title: Activation-Conditioned Quantization Profile Manager and Runtime Fallback Strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an activation-conditioned quantization profile manager that generates per-layer and per-channel INT8 profiles with SmoothQuant-inspired cross-layer activation/weight rebalancing. The manager must produce portable profile artifacts that the runtime can consume to select optimized fused kernels or fall back to generic kernels when accuracy or latency SLOs would be violated. This ticket covers the calibration harness (data collection, activation histograms, per-channel scale derivation), profile serialization format, runtime kernel selector + fallback policy, CI/regression tests and evaluation dashboards. Aim is to reduce quantization-induced accuracy regressions while keeping tail latency within target for production inference workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can produce a per-model profile (channels + rescale maps) on a single v100/rtx A6000 in <= 45 minutes for the representative sample set
Accuracy regression on canonical eval suites is < 0.5% relative to fp16 baseline for top-10 tasks (LM perplexity, QA F1, classification accuracy)
99th percentile tail latency penalty from using fused compensated kernels is < 10% compared to current fp16 runtime under the same batching SLO
Runtime exposes a kernel selection switch that allows canarying fused compensated kernels and automatic rollback to generic INT8 kernels when observed accuracy or latency thresholds are exceeded
Unit tests for profile serialization and deserialization, and integration tests exercising runtime fallback are added to CI with passing status
Documentation for profile format, calibration CLI, and rollout steps added to the internal Confluence page
steps: Design profile schema (v1) and storage sidecar format for model packages
Implement calibration harness: dataset shard sampling, activation probes, channel histogram collector
Compute per-channel scale and cross-layer rescale map; provide conservative defaults for low-sample channels
Export profile and a lightweight verifier that computes estimated accuracy impact
Runtime: implement kernel selector that reads profile and prefers fused compensated kernels; add telemetry hooks for per-request accuracy signals and latency metrics
Add fallback policy engine: threshold-driven automatic rollback and manual overrides in Console
CI: add golden evaluation set, regression thresholds, and nightly calibration runs; wire into PR gating
Perf validate on dedicated capacity (A100 fleet), record dashboards, and iterate on kernel micro-optimizations
Ship docs, merge PRs, and plan canary rollout for 5% of hosted traffic
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: Spike completed — collected activation distributions for 3 representative transformer models (small/medium/large) using 2k prompt samples each. Observed long-tailed channel distributions in early layers.
2025-01-20: Design doc uploaded (see links). Decided to store profile as a compact floating-point table with per-channel multipliers and a schema version to allow safe runtime upgrades.
2025-01-24: Prototype exporter implemented (PR #4021). Produces profiles and a lightweight verifier that runs on CPU. Initial verification shows <0.3% perplexity delta on one medium model.

2025-01-27: Review with Runtime team — major trade-off: storing per-channel maps increases model package size by ~2-4%. Runtime will lazily load maps to avoid memory pressure. Need to add a memory cap guard in kernel selector.
2025-01-30: Kernel team landed fused compensated kernel micro-benchmarks on A100 (PR #4089). Measured 6-8% latency overhead in worst-case microbenchmarks but improved accuracy vs base int8.
2025-02-02: Added CI job prototype that runs profile generation on a nightly job against sample corpus. Next steps: integrate automatic rollback telemetry and Console controls for canary percentage.
release_notes: Adds activation-conditioned INT8 profiling and a runtime kernel selector with automatic fallback. Initial rollout gated to canary traffic and enabled via Console feature flag.
